newsitem.title: CHINA: Hopewell seen hit by Bangkok rail delay.
newsitem.headline: Hopewell seen hit by Bangkok rail delay.

text.p: Hopewell Holdings Ltd's inability to complete Bangkok's mass transit system as planned will make financing the troubled project more difficult and could hurt the company's bottom line, analysts said on Friday.
"We rank the stock a 'trading buy' but now we are revaluating our recommendation," said Leon Chik, research analyst at HSBC James Capel.

Hopewell said on Friday it was unable to complete its long-delayed Bangkok Elevated Rail Train System (BERTS) project as planned due to the decline in Thailand's economy and the de facto devaluation of the baht.
The baht has depreciated 15-20 percent since July 2 when the Bank of Thailand said it would float the currency.
Terry Ip at NZW Securities Asia said the poor Thai economy would made equity and bank financing for the project more difficult.
In its statment, Hopewell said "the international banks, who are committed to the project, now need to reasses the project financing structure."
The company also said said that the downturn of the real estate market and low-fare structure of Thailand's community trains had reduced future revenues and that project costs had increased.
Analysts said if Hopewell was unable to get financing for the project then it might be forced to sell the project at big discount or even write it off completely.
"A write off will shed HK$1.00 per share from its net asset value which is currently at about HK$7.1 per share," Ip said.
In the statement, Hopewell said "the project has had many delays over the years due to frequent changes in government and design changes."
But Hopewall also said it wanted to complete the project and work with the Thai government to overcome financing difficulties.
Hopewell shares were down HK$0.19 at HK$5.15 in early London trade.
In Hong Kong, the stock closed HK$0.15 lower at HK$5.15 after hitting a session high of HK$5.40 on renewed rumours it would be a purchase target of a mainland company or Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd.
"Hopewell needs a partner but the Thai project added uncertainty to the prospects of the company," an analyst with a local brokerage house said.

The US$3.2 billion BERTS project, originally scheduled to be finished by 1999, involves construction of 60 km (37.5 miles) of multi-level railways and highways to relieve chronic traffic congestion in Bangkok.

BZW downgraded Hopewell to sell from speculative buy on Wednesday after the company said it would sell its remaining 19.99 percent stake in Consolidated Electric Power Asia Ltd (CEPA), once the cash cow of the company, to Southern Co Inc.
